title: Memorising is not generalising
summary: Overfitting happens when a model follows training details too closely and does poorly on new examples. Generalising means working on useful new cases.
introduction: Overfitting happens when a model follows training details too closely and does poorly on new examples. Generalising means working on useful new cases. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Overfitting happens when a model follows training details too closely and does poorly on new examples. Generalising means working on useful new cases.
The output is unknown. A lookup table can repeat stored answers but has no rule here for input 4. This illustrates a limit of memorising.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Explain why perfect recall of three rows does not prove a useful prediction rule.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not choose a model only by its training score.
